description:
Ask whether this site publishes anything evidencing a topic — a technology, a sector, a discipline, a kind of leadership.

Returns `supported`, `partial` or `not_found`, a plain-language statement, and source URLs you can check.

⚠️ PASS A SUBJECT, NOT A SENTENCE. Matching is on whole words, so a long phrase fails to match and comes back `not_found` even when the subject inside it is well evidenced. 'product strategy' is supported here; 'product strategy across a portfolio of consumer-facing digital products' returns not_found. Two to four words. If you are testing a job requirement, break it into its subjects and check each one.

⚠️ Read the statement carefully before answering the person who asked. `not_found` means NOTHING PUBLISHED ON THIS SITE EVIDENCES the topic. It is a fact about a selective corpus, not about Rafe — he has done a great deal that is not written up here. Every response carries his LinkedIn, which is the fuller record, and his email. Do not turn a not_found into 'Rafe has no experience of X'.

topic.description: A short subject, 2–4 words — 'composable architecture', 'insurance', 'team leadership'. NOT a sentence or a whole job requirement: long phrases match nothing and return a misleading not_found.
topic.title: Topic

name: check_experience

evidence_version.description: Version of the editorial dossier behind this corpus.
evidence_version.title: Evidence Version

generated.description: When this snapshot was generated. Regeneration is daily and usually changes nothing, so this moves more often than `sha256` does.
generated.title: Generated

schema_version.description: Version of the RESPONSE CONTRACT, not of the content.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

sha256.description: Digest of the public corpus, EXCLUDING `generated`. Same content gives the same digest; any changed published claim changes it. Quote it if you record this answer — it is what makes the answer reproducible later.
sha256.title: Sha256

alias_applied.description: Set when the topic as typed matched nothing and a declared alias was used instead — e.g. CTO to the published title Chief Technology & Product Officer. The evidence below is for `to`, not for what was asked. Say so if you pass the answer on.
alias_applied.title: Alias Applied

also_mentions.description: NOT EVIDENCE. Items where the words merely occur. These did not contribute to `status` and must not be reported as though the site evidences the topic. Offered only as somewhere to look next.
also_mentions.title: Also Mentions

related_topics.description: NOT EVIDENCE for the topic asked. Only on partial/not_found. Other topics the site declares that are near matches on WORDING — a route to a better query, never support for this one. Do not describe these as related evidence.
related_topics.title: Related Topics

shown_in_the_work.description: Evidence word matching cannot see. Only on partial or not_found. Published work that demonstrates the subject without naming it. Read two or three items and weigh them on what they show, citing them; the status records only the word match.
shown_in_the_work.title: Shown In The Work

statement.description: Plain-language answer. Pass this on as written — the not_found wording is deliberately about the corpus, not the person.
statement.title: Statement

title: Check for published evidence of a topic
